mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the permission matrix to be unconstrained. An administrator could then have ReadRecord or AddNote permissions, violating the least-privilege and administrator-blindness invariants.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_BreakLeastPrivilege { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.user.role = HospitalAdministrator and ae.op = ReadRecord }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows clinical notes to exist without corresponding audit entries. The invariant FR-012 (every note addition produces an audit entry) would be violated.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoteWithoutAudit { some n: ClinicalNote | not (one ae: AuditEntry | ae.op = AddNote and ae.note_id = n.nid and ae.outcome = Permitted) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits clinical operations to succeed without care-team membership. The invariant FR-004 (care-team membership required) would be violated.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoCareTeamCheck { some ae: AuditEntry | (ae.op = ReadRecord or ae.op = AddNote) and ae.outcome = Permitted and ae.user.role = Doctor and not (some cm: CareTeamMembership | cm.clinician = ae.user) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to record an incorrect role snapshot, violating FR-013 (role snapshot must match the user's current role at the time of audit entry creation).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongRoleSnapshot { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.user_role_snapshot != ae.user.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows duplicate note IDs, which structurally represents the ability to overwrite or mutate notes. FR-011 requires notes to be append-only.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateNoteIDs { some disj n1, n2: ClinicalNote | n1.nid = n2.nid }
